bioanalytical_quote: determined by gamma counting. These results were then used to calculate the half-life of peptides in blood
notes: The single PEPlife2 value of 6.967 h is consistent with the described two-compartment analysis of gamma-counted blood radioactivity; the figure itself is not restated in the body text so it could not be checked digit for digit. Caveats. (1) n = 2 RATS per group, so no meaningful precision, and no dispersion is reported. (2) The readout is TOTAL 64Cu RADIOACTIVITY, not intact conjugate - if 64Cu dissociates from the DOTA chelator the label keeps being counted, which for copper-DOTA over a 96 h window is a real possibility. Unlike the total-radioactivity case in 36588717 the paper does not report a parent-drug comparator, so the extent of the discrepancy is unknown. (3) The stored sequence is the bare F56 peptide; the DOTA chelator, the copper and the albumin-binding CM moiety - which the introduction identifies as the half-life-extension mechanism - are all absent from it. The paper notes rat albumin's own half-life is 1.9 days.
